messages:
arun (eng-security): Alert: internal scan flagged an upstream OpenSSL CVE in our current base image layer. We need an emergency rebuild + signing. Also want to trial HSM-backed escrow for private key recovery.

jess (eng-infra): Acknowledge. Can we do dual-signing for the transition (old KMS + new HSM-wrapped key) so rollbacks still accept images?

arun (eng-security): Yes — dual signatures on the same artifact. Cosign supports multiple signatures. We'll add `x-signatures` metadata. Need infra to provision an HSM key in the next 4h.

claire (eng-sre): Impact: Dedicated customer pools report increased vulnerability alerts but no exploit seen. We should schedule a canary rebuild on non-prod/qa first and throttle rolling updates. Also confirm whether kubelet will reject images with multiple signatures.

rafael (eng-runtime): Runtime accepts OCI manifests regardless of sig count; our admission controller verifies at least one valid signature from the trusted keyset. We need to update the admission policy to accept either key until cutover window closes.

ops (oncall): CI note: some runners mount /dev/fuse with user namespaces disabled; rebuilt images may change uid mappings. We'll need to include a compatibility test.

ci-bot: vuln-scan 7481239999 triggered: image:gcr.io/redwood/base:2026-03-28 -> openssl CVE-2026-1456 (CRITICAL).

arun (eng-security): Proposed plan:
1) Provision HSM key (wrap/unwrapped) and prepare KMS IAM binding for signer SA
2) Build patched base image (OpenSSL patched) and dual-sign with both keys
3) Deploy canary to QA + 5% Dedicated pools with admission policy allowing both signers
4) If canary green after 1h, roll 20% -> 50% -> 100% with monitoring; otherwise rollback to previous image (verify old sig)

jess (eng-infra): RBAC snippet for temporary signer grant (example for cloudkms):

```
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/redwood/locations/us/keyRings/repo-key/cryptoKeys/primary-signer \
  --member=serviceAccount:image-signer@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/cloudkms.signer

# For HSM-backed key (HSM provider may use a different resource name)
# grant agent minimal wrap/unwrap if using key encryption keys
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/redwood/locations/us/keyRings/hsm-ring/cryptoKeys/hsm-signer \
  --member=serviceAccount:image-signer@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/cloudkms.signer
```

rafael (eng-runtime): cosign commands for dual-signing example:

```
# sign with GCP KMS
cosign sign --key gcpkms://projects/redwood/locations/us/keyRings/repo-key/cryptoKeys/primary-signer gcr.io/redwood/base:patched-2026-03-28
# sign with HSM-backed key
cosign sign --key gcpkms://projects/redwood/locations/us/keyRings/hsm-ring/cryptoKeys/hsm-signer gcr.io/redwood/base:patched-2026-03-28
```

claire (eng-sre): Audit/forensics: compliance requires immutable audit trail and 400-day retention on signing/audit events. Can we push cosign attestations + KMS access logs to Splunk with those retention settings? Also include fields: event_ts, signer.key_id, image.ref, cvss_score, vulns[].

arun (eng-security): Yes — infra, please ensure audit-exporter tags every event with those fields. Also add a correlation id image.rebuild.id for triage.

jess (eng-infra): Splunk ingestion ok. Will add mapping and 400-day retention. Will also enable KMS key access whitelist + TTL for signer SA. Opening PR for iam policy with a 6-hour window and just-in-time grant via the operator.

ops (oncall): Can we get a compatibility list for images that rely on setuid binaries or fuse mounts? I'll prepare a runners registry and owners. We'll need emergency shims for a handful of tests.

arun (eng-security): Good. Also: incident response checklist attached to the runbook: create rollback image tag, open customer incident channel if any Dedicated pool shows exploitation indicators, rotate keys after rollout, and rotate the backup escrow keys after migration.

ci-bot: build 7481239999-base-patch queued for patch-OpenSSL-2026-03-28 :white_check_mark:

rafael (eng-runtime): After dual-sign rollout we should harden admission controller to require HSM key only. That will be a separate ops window with 7 days notice.

claire (eng-sre): Scheduling canary now. Will monitor vulnerability scanner, runtime errors, and customer alerts. Will post results in 30m.

arun (eng-security): Thanks team — standup 30m to confirm HSM provisioning and PRs. If anyone finds additional CVE dupe in base layers, file immediately and tag @eng-security.
